messages:
morgan: heads up, our vuln scanner picked up an OpenSSL CVE that touches both ubuntu:22.04-based and alpine:3.18-based base images. can we triage and set a patch priority?

jamie: which cve id and severity? need that for SLA math.

morgan: CVE-2026-1428, CVSS 8.1 (remote key-exchange flaw in libssl). scanner shows packages in libssl1.1 (ubuntu) and libssl (alpine/musl).

ops-bot: automated-finding: image-scan /images/redwood/*:base -> CVE-2026-1428 (HIGH). exposed in hosted-api-prod, model-runtime-prod, and a few internal CI runners.

ben: prioritize by customer impact: hosted-api-prod first, then model-runtime-prod, then internal. Hosted has public endpoints and high traffic. also consider arm64 builders (we run arm64 for some customers).

sara: agree. two operational asks: (1) who signs/promotes the rebuilt images? we need an RBAC change so only image-signer group + release-bot SA can cosign/push. (2) KMS usage: use our HSM-backed key for cosign; rotate key after the incident.

alex: proposed rollout plan: rebuild alpine & ubuntu base images with patched openssl, run smoke + model-serving health check, canary to 5% traffic for 2 hours, then 25% for 6 hours, full cutover if no regressions.

maria: add load and long-tail QA: run kv-cache heavy traffic for 30m, and run the nightly embedded eval suite — we've seen regressions with musl before.

jamie: technical notes: alpine glibc vs musl — this CVE is in libssl, not glibc. still need to validate compatibility for any native wheels (nvidia/container-runtime libs). test matrix: ubuntu-x86_64, ubuntu-arm64, alpine-x86_64, alpine-arm64.

sec-bot: exploit maturity: proof-of-concept published. recommend high urgency.

ben: timeline request: can infra produce pinned builds and attestations by Wed 09:00 PST? we should aim for a patch window Wed 09:00-13:00 PST if CI completes earlier.

release-bot: created epic: infra/eng-security/baseimage-cve-2026-1428 (link: https://go/release/infra/2026-1428). assigned to @alex @maria @sara.

sara: RBAC details: create group "image-signer" (SAML mapped), give push/cosign permission to staging registry and prod promotion only via release-bot workflow. Add audit log filter on registry: log all sign/push events to secure-audit project with 1yr retention.

alex: cosign snippet for KMS signing in CI:
```
COSIGN_KMS_URI=awskms://arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/abcd-efgh
cosign sign --kms $COSIGN_KMS_URI registry.redwood.com/base:patched-2026-1428
```

maria: regression checklist (minimum): unit tests, smoke start/stop, GPU infer sanity, kv-cache warmup, per-route latency checks, model output diffs on 10 eval prompts. if any fail -> rollback to previous digest + notify oncall.

jamie: note on dependencies: besides openssl bump, pin transitive packages that pull old libssl (e.g., libpq builds). rebuild container layers top-to-bottom to avoid stale cached libssl in intermediate layers.

morgan: decision summary: 1) priority = hosted-api-prod, 2) build & sign patched ubuntu+alpine images for x86_64 & arm64, 3) RBAC: image-signer group + release-bot only, 4) canary plan 5% -> 25% -> full with 2h/6h checks, 5) patch window Wed 09:00-13:00 PST, 6) audit logs to secure-audit with 1y retention, 7) rollback plan defined.

ben: +1. please add exact playbook steps to the epic before Wed. I can coordinate pager coverage.

maria: I'll add the QA checklist and test jobs to the epic. tagging infra for build capacity.

sara: I'll open the RBAC PR and KMS key access policy change, CC security-review.

sec-bot: monitoring: create alert if canary error-rate > 1% or 99th latency increases >50ms during rollout.

morgan: thanks all — will kick off the epic and ping again once first builds are ready.
